messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and connection resets observed in aws-us-west-2 affecting Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Aggregate 5xx rate ~8% for the last 5m. Pager triggered. Runbook: /runbooks/aws-nlb-failures.

Liz: I'm on it, pulling metrics and traces now. Confirming both hosted endpoints and several dedicated GPU pools showing latency spikes and 5xx.

Sam: seeing NLB target health flapping on us-west-2 targets, lots of connection resets and conntrack errors on our edge fleet: "ENOBUFS" and "conntrack: table full" in logs. CloudWatch shows TargetConnectionError and TLS handshake resets.

Rafael: tagging in. @sam please handoff to oncall SRE for routing fallback.

Rafael: taking pager. First actions: 1) apply cross-region routing preference away from us-west-2, 2) start draining Dedicated pools in us-west-2, 3) open AWS support SR.

Liz: Proposed immediate mitigations: a) add emergency route policy route-2026-usw2-failover to prefer us-east-1, b) reduce concurrent connection limits per host in the proxy to lower conntrack pressure, c) enable client-side exponential backoff for 5xx to reduce fanout.

Sam: pushing route policy now. Command: `curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/route-policies -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -d '{"policy":"route-2026-usw2-failover","priority":900,"regions_preference":["us-east-1","eu-west-1"]}'` -> 200 OK.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: route-policy route-2026-usw2-failover canary -> 10% traffic. Canary successful.

Liz: Telemetry update: us-west-2 p95 latency still high (~780ms) but 5xx rate dropped from 8% -> 3% after canary. Continuing rollout to 50%.

Tara: Support triage: list of customers on Dedicated in us-west-2: AcmeCorp-prod, Finlytics-proxy, HealthAI-stage. Marking those as impacted, preparing outbound comms.

Rafael: Draining Dedicated-GPU-UsWest2-01 now. Set desired capacity to 0, migrating jobs to Dedicated-GPU-Useast1-03. Watch for client reconnect flaps.

Sam: Observability note: Datadog log ingestion is delayed due to downstream Kinesis throttling; we have partial log gaps. Rely on internal aggregated metrics for now. Filed obs ticket to vendor.

Liz: Quick config snippet for draining: 
```
kubectl patch deployment dedicated-gpu-usw2 -p '{"spec":{"replicas":0}}'
```
Monitoring pool drain progress.

Rafael: AWS SR opened SR-987654321: NLB connection table exhaustion / unexpected conntrack errors. Support response ETA 30m. Link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/SR-987654321

Sam: Doing full reroute now: increasing route policy rollout to 90%. `routectl promote route-2026-usw2-failover --percent 90` -> OK. Expected final step in 2m.

incident-bot: Telemetry: after 90% reroute, hosted p50 latency global 220ms, us-west-2 traffic 12% of baseline, 5xx rate 0.6%. Dedicated pool success rate 99.6%.

Tara: Draft external status: "We experienced elevated latency and 5xx in us-west-2 due to upstream NLB connection table issues. Traffic was routed to other regions, and Dedicated pools were drained. Minimal customer impact for hosted; a small number of Dedicated customers observed disruptions. Next update in 30 minutes." Posting to status page.

incident-bot: Status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RED-2026-095 — external note posted.

Liz: AWS support replied: investigating NLB control-plane and recommending temporary cross-zone load balancing and submit request for NLB target scaling. They observed unusual conntrack exhaustion on our NAT instances.

Rafael: notes for engineers: consider increasing node conntrack table sizes and enable aggressive socket reuse during cross-region failovers. Also consider autoscaling the egress NAT fleet in us-west-2.

Sam: Handoff plan: I'll stay on the AWS engagement and long tail mitigations. Oncall handoff scheduled at 02:35Z to Sam for the engagement continuity. @nina please take follow-ups at 06:00Z.

Nina: acknowledged, will pick up morning follow-ups and ensure retro is created.

Tara: Customer comms to affected Dedicated customers sent with contact channel and mitigation summary. Support queue flagged high.

Liz: Current state: 5xx reduced to ~0.3% global, us-west-2 now primarily read-only traffic. Elevated latency still present in us-west-2 but non-critical since traffic is routed. Reducing severity to SEV3 and moving to monitoring mode.

Sam: Follow-ups (tickets): 1) Retro: INC-2026-095, 2) eng-runtime: evaluate permanent routing TTLs and cross-region warmup, 3) infra: add conntrack and NLB target metrics to alerts, 4) run failover drill.

incident-bot: Incident marked SEV3 at 03:22Z. Pager cleared for night. Postmortem placeholder created: /incidents/RED-2026-095/postmortem.

Rafael: leaving final note — consider adding a small global cache-warmup token for Dedicated customers during failover to reduce cold-start errors.

Tara: Copy that. Closing this thread for immediate ops. Retro owners assigned.
